First public release. whoas runs CLIs and AI agents as the account you choose:
each login is an encrypted identity in a local vault, and the real CLI runs
against it, one process at a time, without touching the CLI's global session.

## Highlights

**Core**
- Identities sealed with [age](https://age-encryption.org); the master key lives in
  the OS keychain (Secret Service, macOS Keychain), in Windows Credential Manager
  from WSL, or behind a passphrase. A key agent caches it.
- Overlays capture what a CLI's own login writes, so browser logins, SSO and
  refreshed tokens keep working; `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` and friends are never
  written.
- Pick the identity explicitly (`gh@work`), with a profile (`-p work`), a session
  variable or a trusted per-project `.whoas.yaml`. Shims let `gh`, `gcloud`, … (and
  agents that never heard of whoas) resolve it themselves.

**More CLIs**
- `vercel`, `wrangler`, `railway` (experimental) and `docker` adapters.
- `env-token` adapters for API-token CLIs: the token stays in the vault and is
  injected as an env var for one process. 62 built in (`stripe`, `supabase`,
  `terraform`, `openai`, …); `whoas providers --all` lists them.
- Mirrored files a CLI replaces by rename during a run are copied back.

**Claude Code and MCP servers**
- Several Claude subscriptions side by side: `whoas add claude max` stores the
  token from `claude setup-token`.
- `mcp` adapters and `whoas mcp proxy`: a stdio MCP server that forwards to a
  remote one with the project's API key, so it works in any agent (Claude Code,
  Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, opencode, …). `whoas mcp setup` registers it.
  PostHog and Linear are built in.
- A secret can declare a `pattern`; `add` and `import` reject values that do not
  match (Claude tokens are checked).

## Breaking / notable

- The provider name `mcp` is reserved: a user adapter named exactly `mcp` now
  fails to load. Rename it.
- Built-in `forge` removed: Foundry installs a `forge` too.
- `hf` injects `HF_TOKEN` (and removes the legacy `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN`).
- Built-ins `dog`, `grok` and `td` removed: other CLIs use the same names. Keep
  one as a [user adapter](https://github.com/S-kkipie/whoas#adding-a-cli) if you need it.
- The key agent no longer inherits the environment of the process that starts
  it, so tokens injected into a session cannot outlive it there.

## Install

```sh
go install github.com/S-kkipie/whoas/cmd/whoas@v0.3.0
```

Or download the archive for your platform below (Linux and macOS, amd64 and
arm64), check it against `checksums.txt` and put `whoas` on your `PATH`. Then
run `whoas doctor`.

**WSL:** to keep the master key in Windows Credential Manager, put `whoas.exe`
(from the `windows_amd64` zip, `windows_arm64` on Arm) next to the Linux `whoas`
before your first `whoas add`. Native Windows is not supported yet: the Windows
build only ships the keystore helper WSL uses.
